items.title: Kings reportedly discussed Domantas Sabonis trade with Celtics, Pistons
items.content:
Kings reportedly discussed Domantas Sabonis trade with Celtics, Pistons originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

It’s no secret the Kings are in a rebuilding phase, as they look to build around a new, younger core led by the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Darius Acuff Jr.

But as that focus shifts towards the promising rookie, general manager Scott Perry still must figure out what to do with some of Sacramento’s high-paid veterans on long-term deals, namely Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine.

There have been several reports in recent months regarding the Kings’ attempts to trade Sabonis, including unsuccessful discussions with the Toronto Raptors at the NBA trade deadline in February and the Charlotte Hornets prior to the NBA Draft in June. 

And now, as ESPN’s Anthony Slater reported in a story this week, Perry also engaged in trade talks with the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics involving Sabonis, who underwent season-ending knee surgery on Feb. 18.

“Perry visited with restricted free agent center Jalen Duren in early July and explored the idea of a sign-and-trade swap of big men,” Slater wrote, “but the Detroit Pistons balked at the idea of losing Duren for Sabonis, league sources said.

“There were predraft conversations about Sabonis with the Charlotte Hornets (who held pick Nos. 14 and 18) and at least one phone call with the Boston Celtics, team and league sources said, but nothing materialized. In Charlotte’s case, the idea would’ve been to pair Sabonis with point guard LaMelo Ball, but the franchise instead opted to trade Ball for draft picks and lean further into a youth movement.”

The Sacramento Kings are shifting into the Darius Acuff era but still have to manage a leftover layer of veterans next to the younger core

ESPN story https://t.co/1JxmsuUM2B

— Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) August 5, 2026

Duren, a 22-year-old NBA All-Star last season with the Pistons, perhaps would have been a better fit for the Kings’ new timeline with Acuff. But now, it appears Sabonis is set to return to Sacramento for the 2026-27 NBA season.

The veteran big man, who turned 30 in May, is coming off a disappointing year in which he played just 19 games; his 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game all were his lowest marks since his third NBA season in 2018-19.

Slater also reported Sabonis “has expressed a willingness to recommit and buy-in to this season’s team,” citing sources with the Kings. Sabonis still is owed just over $94 million over the final two seasons of his current contract. And though he is eligible for an extension, that isn’t currently on the table, according to Slater.

With LaVine seemingly remaining with the Kings as well, it’s set to be an interesting campaign for Sacramento as the team looks to transition from one core to another.

“I just wanted to let you know that your son is here. He was born today,” Princess wrote to Pierce on Feb. 6, per TMZ. “If you’d like to see him tomorrow, let me know.”

items.title: Terrell Brown Jr. To Sign With Jazz
items.content:
Guard Terrell Brown Jr. has agreed to a contract with the Jazz, agent Daniel Hazan tells NBA insider Chris Haynes (Twitter link).

While the terms of the deal were not disclosed, it’ll likely be a non-guaranteed training camp contract featuring Exhibit 10 language. That would entitle Brown to a bonus if he’s waived before the season begins and spends at least 60 days with Utah’s NBAGL affiliate, the Salt Lake City Stars.

Brown, 28, went undrafted in 2022 after spending his final college season at the University of Washington. The Seattle native has played in the G League for the past four seasons, having suited up for the Memphis Hustle and 2022/23 and the Greensboro Swarm — Charlotte’s affiliate team — since the 2023 offseason.

Brown, who signed Exhibit 10 contracts with the Hornets in 2023 and 2025, averaged 11.9 points, 6.4 assists (against 1.6 turnovers), 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 50 total games (25.7 minutes per contest) for the Swarm last season. He struggled with scoring efficiency, posting a .404/.325/.782 shooting line, but he helped Greensboro win the NBAGL championship in the spring.

In all likelihood Brown will be waived before the season begins and will head to the Stars to open 2026/27. The Jazz currently have 14 players on guaranteed standard contracts, Mo Bamba on a partially guaranteed deal, Harrison Ingram on an Exhibit 10 pact, and all three two-way spots filled. The team will be at 20 players under contract, one shy of the offseason limit, once Brown’s agreement becomes official.
